knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Reduction operators may fail when a dtype/device combination lacks a corresponding backend kernel dispatch or is not explicitly rejected at API validation time.

risk_dimensions.dtype: Low-precision floating-point dtypes such as float16 and bfloat16 on accelerator backends
risk_dimensions.device: CUDA and other accelerator backend dispatch paths

failure_mechanism.description: The API accepts a dtype/device combination, but the backend lacks a corresponding kernel dispatch path or fails to reject the unsupported combination, causing a runtime error.

input_exploration: Vary dtype and device combinations for reduction operations
Include low-precision floating-point dtypes on accelerator devices
Explore reduction APIs across varied shapes, strides, and memory layouts
Probe dtype/backend combinations that may lack kernel support
constraint_awareness: Some reduction operations have hidden dtype/backend dispatch constraints
Unsupported dtype/device combinations may pass API validation and fail later
Backend kernel availability varies by dtype and device
oracle_strategy: Monitor for runtime errors indicating missing kernel dispatch or unsupported dtype
Treat explicit exceptions on valid tensor inputs as dispatch boundary failures

transferability.reason: Reduction and similar dtype-sensitive operators rely on backend dispatch, so the principle of probing dtype/device combinations for missing kernel support applies broadly across many APIs.

important_considerations: Probe reduction APIs with dtype/device combinations at and beyond documented support boundaries
Do not assume API layer validation catches unsupported backend dispatch paths
Include low-precision dtypes on accelerator devices
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that systematically vary dtype and device for reduction APIs
Combine floating-point dtypes such as float16 and bfloat16 with CUDA and other backends
Use generic error detection to classify runtime dispatch failures
